subject: Token rate targets + host-split analysis and next steps
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Lucas Chen <lucas@nimhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Token rate targets + host-split analysis and next steps

Hi Lucas —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap and a proposed pricing posture so we can align on a pilot:

Call highlights (from our side)
- Primary use: clinical triage + summarization for inbound patient messages (short prompts, average response length ~350 tokens).
- Expected steady-state: ~120M tokens / month. Burst windows up to ~250M for peak events.
- Latency target: 400–800ms 95th for single-turn queries.
- Data: PHI-sensitive, needs HIPAA controls + US region hosting.

Commercial ask — what we discussed on call
- Volume band: 100–150M tokens/mo initially; goal to scale to 1B+ in 12 months depending on accuracy.
- NimHealth target unit price (you mentioned) ~ $12–16 / 1M tokens as a shaded range.

Redwood quick benchmark & suggested offer (engineered to be competitive vs public hosts while preserving margin):
- OpenAI (public hosted, general-purpose): ~ $60 / 1M (for their most capable multi-turn model we compared)
- Anthropic (hosted): ~ $45 / 1M
- Generic open-model hosts (managed ggml/quantized offerings): ~ $18–25 / 1M depending on latency and SLA
- Redwood projected hosted list price: $14 / 1M (reserved commit pricing to start: $9 / 1M at 1B+ tokens/month)
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU, quantized stack): estimated delivered cost to NimHealth ~ $6 / 1M (if you want capacity isolation + lowest unit economics)

Notes on the numbers: these are commercial-facing per-1M-token comparisons (not our internal marginal compute costs). They reflect model-family equivalence, SLA, and typical prefix lengths for triage workloads. We can build a short workup showing how those numbers change with average prompt/response size, caching, batching, and KV reuse.

Next steps I propose
1) Can you confirm expected steady-state and burst monthly tokens (a single row CSV is fine) — I attached a quick template.
2) Confirm whether the $/1M target range you mentioned ($12–16) is a hard constraint or a negotiation starting point.
3) If acceptable, we’ll send a 30-day pilot commercial (commit + pilot pricing) and a simple SOC/HIPAA addendum for legal.

I attached a token profile template and an internal price workup — see the second tab for a detailed unit-econ sensitivity table.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199

---
Attachments: nimhealth_token_profile.csv (template), redwood_host_price_workup_v1.xlsx (pricing workup)

From: Lucas Chen <lucas@nimhealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@nimhealth.com
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 11:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Token rate targets + host-split analysis and next steps

Olga —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Volume confirmation
- Current pilot target: 120M tokens/month (avg) — as you estimated.
- Expected steady growth: 350–400M tokens/month by month 6 if the accuracy holds.

2) Budget sensitivity
- The $12–16 / 1M band is what product leadership used as a budgeting assumption; procurement will push for lower if there are multi-quarter commit discounts. Our informal internal target is $12 / 1M but we can tolerate up to $16 for a managed solution that meets HIPAA + <800ms 95th latency.

3) Key gating items
- SOC2 + HIPAA attestation and ability to sign a BA (hipaa BA).
- Data residency: must stay in us-east-1 or us-west-2.
- PO process: procurement needs a 30-day net invoice and a standard MSSA with a one-off BA addendum.

We are open to a two-phase commercial: pilot (30 days, up to 150M tokens) at a slightly higher pilot rate, then a reserved commit for production with stepped discounts.

Can you send a sample pilot quote with (a) pilot rate, (b) production commit tiers, and (c) what triggers the $9 / 1M reserved rate you mentioned? Also include a short note on expected latency on Hosted vs Dedicated in practice.

If you want, Marcus or Karthik can run through the unit-econ slide with my procurement counterpart next week.

Best,
Lucas
VP Product, NimHealth
lucas@nimhealth.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lucas Chen <lucas@nimhealth.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 12:20:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: Token rate targets + host-split analysis and next steps

Lucas —

Thanks for the clarity. Quick response to the asks and a small unit-econ sketch so procurement has line-items to review.

Pilot & commercial outline (high level) - Pilot (30 days):
  - Cap: 150M tokens; pilot rate: $20 / 1M tokens (keeps pilot economics simple; includes priority support and SOC2/HIPAA attachment)
  - Deliverables: deployment in us-west-2, logging + token-level cost dashboard access, 95th latency SLA target (best-effort)

- Production reserved tiers (monthly commit):
  - 100–250M: $14 / 1M
  - 250–999M: $11 / 1M
  - 1B+: $9 / 1M (requires 12-month commit and minimum monthly throughput guarantee)

Unit economics (assumptions we use internally)
- Model family: quantized Llama-family equivalent in inference (latency tuned)
- Delivered infra + software amortized cost to Redwood: ~$4–6 / 1M at 100–250M volumes; drops to ~$2–3 / 1M at 1B+ due to utilization and amortization of reserved capacity
- Commercial price to NimHealth at 100–250M: $14 / 1M => Redwood margin to support SRE/observability/legal: ~ 40–60% depending on support level

Latency notes
- Hosted (shared): typical 95th in our tests for triage workloads ~ 350–700ms depending on prompt lengths and KV reuse; production SLA available with committed burst capacity.
- Dedicated (reserved GPUs): consistent sub-500ms 95th; preferred if you have hard latency SLOs and want the best unit economics for sustained high-volume usage.

We will attach a one-page pilot quote and a two-page unit-econ appendix to the HubSpot deal; I’ve also put a short checklist for procurement.

Next step: Olga — can you confirm if we should send the formal pilot quote to procurement@nimhealth.com and whether a one-week signature window is required for the pilot?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Karthik / Olga —

This looks good and actionable. Procurement prefers the pilot quote to be explicit about (1) termination after 30 days if KPIs not met and (2) a clear path to the 12-month commit that triggers the $9 / 1M rate.

Please send the pilot quote to procurement@nimhealth.com and loop me. We should be able to sign within 5 business days if the BA is in place. Also, include an appendix that shows cost sensitivity if average response size goes from 350 tokens to 600 tokens (that will likely be our worst-case).

Requesting PO process details: we prefer Net 30 invoices; include legal contact for BA negotiation.

Thanks — we’re ready to proceed once the quote + BA are present.

Best,
Lucas
VP Product, NimHealth
